channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Attacks in Gulf Threaten to Reignite Conflict
item.description: US warships shot down missiles and drones targeting ships in the Strait of Hormuz. The United Arab Emirates blamed Iran for a drone attack, escalating tensions in the region. U. S.

item.title: US strikes Iranian fast boats as Iran attacks UAE oil facility
item.description: US military protected a US-flagged Maersk vessel as it exited the Strait of Hormuz. The vessel's safe passage came after US strikes on Iranian fast boats that attacked an UAE oil facility.

item.title: Meta taps Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan for El Paso data center deal, Bloomberg News reports
item.description: Meta has chosen Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan for a data center deal in El Paso, according to Bloomberg News. The deal's terms have not been disclosed. Meta taps Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan for El Paso data center deal, Bloomberg News reports.

item.title: OPEC+ Hikes Oil Production Quotas Without Mentioning UAE Pull-Out
item.description: OPEC+ increased oil production quotas without addressing the United Arab Emirates' reported pull-out. The group's untapped reserves are mainly located in the Gulf region. Untapped OPEC+ reserves are mainly located in the Gulf region.

item.title: Attacks in Strait of Hormuz, Gulf region imperil fragile U.S.-Iran ceasefire
item.description: Recent attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf region threaten a fragile US-Iran ceasefire. The incidents have raised concerns about the stability of the region. Attacks in Strait of Hormuz, Gulf region imperil fragile U. S.-Iran ceasefire The Washington Post.

item.title: The US fights to reopen the Strait of Hormuz as the UAE comes under attack in a test of Iran truce
item.description: The US military is working to reopen the Strait of Hormuz after the United Arab Emirates came under attack, testing a truce with Iran. The US is seeking to restore shipping through the strategic waterway.

item.title: Armed man shot by U.S. Secret Service near White House
item.description: A man was shot by the U. S. Secret Service near the White House, shortly after Vice-President J. D. Vance's motorcade passed by. The incident occurred near the National Mall. The U. S. Secret Service Deputy Director Matthew Quinn confirmed the details.

item.title: Zelenskyy rallies partners on defence, sanctions and diplomacy at EPC summit
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy rallied partners on defence, sanctions, and diplomacy at the European Political Community summit. He urged collective action against Russia. The summit aimed to strengthen unity among European nations.

item.title: World Must Hold U.S. Responsible for Making Strait of Hormuz Unsafe
item.description: Iran stated that the world must hold the U. S. responsible for making the Strait of Hormuz unsafe. The U. S. presence in the region was deemed a threat. Iran's stance was reported by iranpress. com.

item.title: Hormuz tensions push ceasefire to the brink as Trump threatens Iran
item.description: The US encouraged ships to pass through the Hormuz Strait despite Iran's control claims. Trump threatened Iran over the situation. US military says it is encouraging ships to pass through Hormuz Strait, but Iran says it is in full control of waterway.

item.title: Is Israel’s interception of the Global Sumud Flotilla legal?
item.description: Spain condemned Israel's detention of two activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla as an abduction. The incident raised questions about Israel's interception of the flotilla. The Spanish government expressed its disapproval.

item.title: Modi’s BJP poised to take control in India’s West Bengal
item.description: India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling BJP is poised to gain control of West Bengal. The BJP's expected victory marks a significant shift in the state's politics. Modi's party is likely to wrest control from the current ruling party.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine declare competing ceasefires
item.description: Russia declared a May 9 truce, while Ukraine claimed its adversary fears Ukrainian drones. Moscow's declaration of May 9 truce comes as Kyiv revels in its adversary's 'fear' of Ukrainian drones.

item.title: Police clash with protesters after ICE arrest in New York
item.description: New York police clashed with protesters outside a hospital where a man arrested by ICE agents was being treated. The incident occurred on a busy street in Manhattan. Police clashed with protesters outside a New York hospital where a man arrested by ICE agents was being treated.

item.title: Why U.S. troops are stationed in Germany, and what happens if some leave
item.description: US troops are stationed in Germany, with potential moves elsewhere under discussion. NPR's Mary Louise Kelly talks with Jeff Rathke, president of the American-German Institute, about U. S. troops stationed in Germany, and what happens if President Trump moves some of them elsewhere.

item.title: Elon Musk To Pay $1.5 Million To Settle Twitter Stake Case
item.description: Elon Musk's trust will pay a $1.5 million civil penalty to settle a case over his Twitter stake. The payment resolves a dispute over Musk's ownership of the social media platform.

item.title: Moscow rehearses V-Day parade marking WWII victory
item.description: Russia rehearsed its Victory Day parade and declared a ceasefire with Ukraine. Moscow rehearses V-Day parade marking WWII victory.

item.title: Trump Obsesses Over Ballroom as Iran War Ceasefire Unravels
item.description: A ceasefire in the Iran war is unraveling, amid other concerns. Trump Obsesses Over Ballroom as Iran War Ceasefire Unravels The Daily Beast.

item.title: Associated Press, Washington Post, Reuters Win 2025 Pulitzer Awards
item.description: The New York Times won three Pulitzer awards, while Reuters took home two prizes in the 2025 ceremony. The Associated Press also received recognition in the journalism awards. The New York Times won three of the coveted prizes, Reuters won two Pulitzer awards.

item.title: Modi's party takes control of India's West Bengal in key state election
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party took control of West Bengal in a key state election, strengthening Modi's political position midway through his third term. The outcome is expected to strengthen Modi's political position midway through his third term.
